Manage plans: the work of a feature broken into tasks for agents.

A plan is YAML: a goal, and tasks, each a prompt for an agent with the tasks it waits for; or a big plan broken into smaller plans, each a PR. wdx help plans says how to write one. Every change of a plan is a new revision, made on the revision it was read at, as for docs.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`wdx plan archive`](#wdx-plan-archive) | Archive a done or cancelled plan, leaving it out of plan list |
| [`wdx plan cancel`](#wdx-plan-cancel) | Cancel a running or paused plan: its agents stop, and it cannot run again |
| [`wdx plan copy`](#wdx-plan-copy) | Create a draft from a plan's latest revision, to run again or start from |
| [`wdx plan create`](#wdx-plan-create) | Create a plan from its YAML |
| [`wdx plan get`](#wdx-plan-get) | Print a plan's YAML, or write it to a file to change |
| [`wdx plan history`](#wdx-plan-history) | List a plan's revisions |
| [`wdx plan list`](#wdx-plan-list) | List a project's plans |
| [`wdx plan pause`](#wdx-plan-pause) | Pause a running plan: nothing new starts, and tasks at work go on and land |
| [`wdx plan remove`](#wdx-plan-remove) | Delete a plan and all its revisions |
| [`wdx plan rename`](#wdx-plan-rename) | Rename a plan |
| [`wdx plan resume`](#wdx-plan-resume) | Resume a paused plan, which starts what its pause held back |
| [`wdx plan run`](#wdx-plan-run) | Run a draft plan: an agent for each task, landing on the plan's branch |
| [`wdx plan set`](#wdx-plan-set) | Change a plan's folder, or how many tasks a running or paused plan runs at once |
| [`wdx plan status`](#wdx-plan-status) | Show what a plan defines and how its run goes: its goal, and its tasks or plans in DAG order |
| [`wdx plan task done`](#wdx-plan-task-done) | Say a task of a running plan is done, so that it lands on the plan's branch |
| [`wdx plan task get`](#wdx-plan-task-get) | Show a plan's task: its state, agent and worktree, prompt and summary |
| [`wdx plan task land`](#wdx-plan-task-land) | Land a land\_failed task again, once you dealt with what stopped it |
| [`wdx plan task retry`](#wdx-plan-task-retry) | Run a failed or land\_failed task again, keeping its worktree and commits |
| [`wdx plan task skip`](#wdx-plan-task-skip) | Skip a pending, failed or land\_failed task: what waits for it goes on without it |
| [`wdx plan unarchive`](#wdx-plan-unarchive) | Show an archived plan in plan list again |
| [`wdx plan update`](#wdx-plan-update) | Write a plan's YAML as a new revision |

## wdx plan archive

Archive a done or cancelled plan, leaving it out of plan list.

```sh
wdx plan archive (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

Nothing else of it changes: its branch, its worktree, its summaries and its history stay, and plan list `--all` shows it.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# A plan of the project you are in
wdx plan archive --name sso

# By id, as JSON
wdx plan archive --id doc-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The plan. With `--json`: {"result": "archived", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `archived` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_finished`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_finished) | 1 | the plan is not done or cancelled, or a plan it waits for is not done |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan cancel

Cancel a running or paused plan: its agents stop, and it cannot run again.

```sh
wdx plan cancel (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--yes] [flags]
```

Its worktrees holding work stay as ordinary worktrees, the others are removed, and its branch stays: nothing done is lost. You are asked first, as a cancelled plan cannot go on; `--yes` answers in advance, and with `--json`, or without a terminal, it is required.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--yes` |  | cancel it without asking |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`
- with `--json`: one of `--yes`

### Examples

```sh
# Cancel a plan of the project you are in
wdx plan cancel --name sso

# From a script
wdx plan cancel --id doc-1a2b3c4d --yes --json
```

### Output

The plan, cancelled. With `--json`: {"result": "cancelled", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `cancelled`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#cancelled) | 1 | the question was answered no |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_running) | 1 | the plan is not running or paused |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan copy

Create a draft from a plan's latest revision, to run again or start from.

```sh
wdx plan copy (--id <id> | --name <name>) --new-name <name> [--folder <folder>] [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

A plan runs once: running it again is a copy, then plan run. The plan can be in any state, archived too. The copy is checked as plan create checks a new plan, in the same project, and has none of the plan's history, run, branch or worktrees. It goes in `--folder`, or the plan's folder.

A plan of plans is copied to run again what is left: with each plan it lists that is not done, as drafts in the same folder, each named with -&lt;n&gt;, the first n from 2 free for all of them (auth-b-2, auth-c-2). The copy lists those, without its afters on the plans done, whose work is in the default branch once landed. With every plan done, nothing is copied.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--folder <folder>` |  | folder of the copy (default: the plan's) |
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--new-name <name>` |  | name of the copy |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--new-name` is required
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Run a plan of the project you are in again
wdx plan copy --name sso --new-name sso-2

# In another folder, as JSON
wdx plan copy --name sso --new-name sso-2 --folder /later --json

# A plan of plans, with its plans
wdx plan copy --name auth --new-name auth-2
```

### Output

The copy, at revision 1; a plan of plans' copy, with the copies of its plans not done. With `--json`: {"result": "created", "plan": {...}, "dropped": [], "moved": []}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `created`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`invalid_name`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_name) | 1 | the name is not allowed |
| [`invalid_plan`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_plan) | 1 | the plan's YAML has problems: details.problems lists them |
| [`name_taken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#name_taken) | 1 | something else has this name |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan create

Create a plan from its YAML.

```sh
wdx plan create --name <name> (--path <file> | --path -) [--folder <folder>] [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

The YAML is the file `--path` names, or stdin with `--path` -, which an AI uses to send it with no file to write; wdx help plans says how to write it. Every problem in it is reported with its line, and nothing is created. Names have letters, numbers and - only, at most 95, and are unique among a project's plans whatever their case; a doc may have the same name.

An after another path already covers is dropped, and said so: the plan is stored without it.

Its folder, / by default, is only where tide shows it, cleaned and checked as a doc's (wdx doc `--help`). A plan of plans and the plans it lists share one: those it lists move to its folder, and moved names them.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--folder <folder>` |  | folder tide shows it in, such as /hub (default: /, the top) |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan |
| `--path <file>` |  | file holding the plan's YAML, - for stdin |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--name` is required
- `--path` is required
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# From a file, in the project you are in
wdx plan create --name sso --path sso.yaml

# In a folder
wdx plan create --name sso --path sso.yaml --folder /hub

# From stdin, as JSON
wdx plan create --project-name app --name sso --path - --json
```

### Output

The plan, at revision 1, each after dropped, and the plans it lists moved to its folder. With `--json`: {"result": "created", "plan": {...}, "dropped": [{"entry": ..., "after": ..., "via": ...}, ...], "moved": [...]}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `created`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`invalid_name`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_name) | 1 | the name is not allowed |
| [`invalid_plan`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_plan) | 1 | the plan's YAML has problems: details.problems lists them |
| [`name_taken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#name_taken) | 1 | something else has this name |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan get

Print a plan's YAML, or write it to a file to change.

```sh
wdx plan get (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--revision <n>] [--out <file> [--overwrite]] [flags]
```

The latest revision unless `--revision` is given, printed byte for byte. With `--out` it is written to a file of yours to edit, then given back with plan update `--base` and the revision it was read at; a file there is replaced only with `--overwrite`. plan status shows what it defines.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--out <file>` |  | file to write it to, read-write, instead of printing it |
| `--overwrite` |  | with `--out`, replace the file if there is one |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--revision <revision>` | `0` | the revision to get (default: the latest) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Print a plan of the project you are in
wdx plan get --name sso

# Write it to a file to change
wdx plan get --name sso --out sso.yaml

# Get it again after it changed
wdx plan get --name sso --out sso.yaml --overwrite

# An earlier revision, as JSON
wdx plan get --id doc-1a2b3c4d --revision 2 --json
```

### Output

The YAML alone; with `--out`, the revision written and where. With `--json`: {"plan": {...}, "revision": ..., "content": "..."}, without content with `--out`

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`path_exists`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#path_exists) | 1 | something is already at the path, as the directory to clone into |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan history

List a plan's revisions.

```sh
wdx plan history (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

Every revision is kept until the plan is removed; plan get `--revision` reads one.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# The revisions of a plan of the project you are in
wdx plan history --name sso

# By id, as JSON
wdx plan history --id doc-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The revisions, latest first, without their YAML. With `--json`: {"revisions": [...]}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan list

List a project's plans.

```sh
wdx plan list [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--all] [flags]
```

Without a project flag, the plans of the project the working directory is in. The archived are left out unless `--all` is given.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` |  | list the archived plans too |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# The plans of the project you are in
wdx plan list

# The archived too
wdx plan list --all

# Of another project, as JSON
wdx plan list --project-name app --json
```

### Output

The plans by folder, then name, without their YAML; an empty list when there are none. With `--json`: {"plans": [...]}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan pause

Pause a running plan: nothing new starts, and tasks at work go on and land.

```sh
wdx plan pause (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

A plan paused while its project is closed stays paused when the project opens.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# A plan of the project you are in
wdx plan pause --name sso

# By id, as JSON
wdx plan pause --id doc-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The plan. With `--json`: {"result": "paused", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `paused` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_running) | 1 | the plan is not running or paused |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan remove

Delete a plan and all its revisions.

```sh
wdx plan remove (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [--yes] [flags]
```

You are asked first, as nothing brings it back; `--yes` answers in advance, and with `--json`, or without a terminal, it is required. A plan a plan of plans lists stays until it is taken out of it; removing a plan of plans leaves the plans it listed as they are, with no parent.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--yes` |  | remove it without asking |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`
- with `--json`: one of `--yes`

### Examples

```sh
# Remove a plan of the project you are in
wdx plan remove --name sso

# From a script
wdx plan remove --id doc-1a2b3c4d --yes --json
```

### Output

The removed plan, as it was before. With `--json`: {"result": "removed", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `removed`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#cancelled) | 1 | the question was answered no |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_in_use`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_in_use) | 1 | a plan of plans lists the plan |
| [`plan_started`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_started) | 1 | the plan has run: only a draft can be changed or run |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan rename

Rename a plan.

```sh
wdx plan rename (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] --new-name <name> [flags]
```

Its id, YAML and revisions stay as they are; changing only the case of its name is a rename. A plan a plan of plans lists keeps its name until it is taken out of it, so that the parent does not name a plan that is not there.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--new-name <name>` |  | the plan's new name |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--new-name` is required
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Rename a plan of the project you are in
wdx plan rename --name sso --new-name sso-login

# By id, as JSON
wdx plan rename --id doc-1a2b3c4d --new-name sso-login --json
```

### Output

The plan's name before and now. With `--json`: {"result": "updated", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_name`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_name) | 1 | the name is not allowed |
| [`name_taken`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#name_taken) | 1 | something else has this name |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_in_use`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_in_use) | 1 | a plan of plans lists the plan |
| [`plan_started`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_started) | 1 | the plan has run: only a draft can be changed or run |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan resume

Resume a paused plan, which starts what its pause held back.

```sh
wdx plan resume (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

Refused while its project is closed, as nothing could run: a plan running when its project closed shows paused, and goes on by itself when the project opens.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# A plan of the project you are in
wdx plan resume --name sso

# By id, as JSON
wdx plan resume --id doc-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The plan. With `--json`: {"result": "resumed", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `resumed` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_running) | 1 | the plan is not running or paused |
| [`project_closed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#project_closed) | 1 | the project is closed |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan run

Run a draft plan: an agent for each task, landing on the plan's branch.

```sh
wdx plan run (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--parallel <n>] [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

Makes the branch plan/&lt;name&gt; at the tip of the project's default branch, then starts an agent for every task whose afters are done, each in a worktree of the plan's, up to `--parallel` at once (the setting plan.parallel when left out). A task's agent says when it is done, with plan task done; its work is then rebased onto the plan's branch, and what waited for it starts. Once every task is done, one worktree is left on the plan's branch, to land as any worktree. A plan runs once, and cannot be changed after.

A plan of plans starts each plan it lists from the default branch once the plans before it are done and their work is in the default branch: landed through wdx, or a PR pulled. Every plan it lists must be a draft whose branch can be made; `--parallel` is each plan's own, so it takes none. A plan it lists whose plans before it are done, but whose work it cannot see in the default branch, waits for you: running that plan is the answer, which also asks gh whether their PR is merged, its merge pulled into the default branch.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--parallel <number>` | `0` | the most tasks it runs at once, a number from 1 to 20 (default: the setting plan.parallel) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# A plan of the project you are in
wdx plan run --name sso

# Two tasks at most at once, as JSON
wdx plan run --name sso --parallel 2 --json

# A plan of plans
wdx plan run --name auth

# A plan it lists that waits for you, once the PR before it is merged and pulled
wdx plan run --name auth-b
```

### Output

The plan, running, and its branch; a plan of plans, and its plans. With `--json`: {"result": "started", "plan": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `started`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`branch_exists`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#branch_exists) | 1 | a new worktree's branch already exists |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_in_use`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_in_use) | 1 | a plan of plans lists the plan |
| [`plan_not_finished`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_finished) | 1 | the plan is not done or cancelled, or a plan it waits for is not done |
| [`plan_not_landed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_landed) | 1 | the work of a plan it waits for is not in the default branch |
| [`plan_started`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_started) | 1 | the plan has run: only a draft can be changed or run |
| [`project_closed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#project_closed) | 1 | the project is closed |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan set

Change a plan's folder, or how many tasks a running or paused plan runs at once.

```sh
wdx plan set (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--parallel <n>] [--folder <folder>] [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

`--parallel`: more start at once when it rises; tasks at work go on when it falls. The setting plan.parallel is the number for every plan whose run sets none.

`--folder`: in any state, cleaned and checked as a doc's (wdx doc `--help`). A plan of plans and the plans it lists move together, whichever is named; moved names the others. With `--parallel`, a plan not running changes neither.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--folder <folder>` |  | folder to move it and its family to, such as /hub; / is the top |
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--parallel <number>` | `0` | the most tasks it runs at once, a number from 1 to 20 |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- at least one of `--parallel` or `--folder`
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Four tasks at once
wdx plan set --name sso --parallel 4

# Move it, and its family, to a folder
wdx plan set --name sso --folder /hub

# As JSON
wdx plan set --name sso --parallel 1 --json
```

### Output

The plan, and the others moved with it. With `--json`: {"result": "updated", "plan": {...}, "moved": [...]}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_running) | 1 | the plan is not running or paused |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan status

Show what a plan defines and how its run goes: its goal, and its tasks or plans in DAG order.

```sh
wdx plan status (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

DAG order lists an entry after everything it waits for, keeping the YAML's order where it is free to: a plan written in order reads as written. Once it runs, each task's state, agent and worktree.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# A plan of the project you are in
wdx plan status --name sso

# By id, as JSON
wdx plan status --id doc-1a2b3c4d --json
```

### Output

The plan's state, goal and constraints, then a row per task or plan. With `--json`: {"plan": {...}, "revision": ..., "definition": {"goal": ..., "constraints": [...], "tasks": [...], "plans": [...]}, "run": {...}}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan task done

Say a task of a running plan is done, so that it lands on the plan's branch.

```sh
wdx plan task done (--agent-id <id> | --plan <name> --task <id>) --summary <text> [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

A task's agent runs it once its work is committed on its branch, naming itself with `--agent-id` $WDX\_AGENT\_ID; a person names the plan and the task. Refused while the task's worktree has changes or files not committed, or is not on the task's branch. The summary is told to the tasks that wait for it. The task's agent is then stopped, and the task lands.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent-id <id>` |  | id of the task's agent, which an agent finds in $WDX\_AGENT\_ID |
| `--plan <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--summary <text>` |  | what was done, in a few lines: text the tasks waiting for it are told |
| `--task <id>` |  | id of the task in the plan |

- `--summary` is required
- at least one of `--agent-id` or `--plan`
- at most one of `--agent-id` or `--task`
- at most one of `--agent-id` or `--project-id`
- at most one of `--agent-id` or `--project-name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`
- all or none of `--plan`, `--task`

### Examples

```sh
# From the task's agent
wdx plan task done --agent-id agent-1a2b3c4d --summary Added_the_table

# From a person, as JSON
wdx plan task done --plan sso --task schema --summary Added_the_table --json
```

### Output

The task, landing. With `--json`: {"result": "landing", "task": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `landing`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`agent_working`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#agent_working) | 1 | an agent is working in the worktree |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_committed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_committed) | 1 | the worktree has files not committed |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_running) | 1 | the plan is not running or paused |
| [`task_state`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#task_state) | 1 | the plan's task is not in a state the request needs |
| [`wrong_branch`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#wrong_branch) | 1 | the worktree is not on the branch the request needs |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

For a conflict or a check you resolved yourself in the task's worktree: commit it on the task's branch first. To have its agent do it, use plan task retry. Refused while an agent is at work in the worktree.

```sh
# Of another project, as JSON

```

The task. With `--json`: {"result": "landing", "task": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `landing`.

### Errors

| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan task retry

Run a failed or land\_failed task again, keeping its worktree and commits.

```sh
wdx plan task retry --plan <name> --task <id> [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] [flags]
```

Its agent is resumed, told what went wrong (it ended, its landing conflicted, or the check failed), and lands the task again with plan task done. With `--fresh`, or when its worktree is gone, a new agent starts instead, named after the attempt, told a previous attempt left its commits. It starts once the plan has room under its parallel, and only while the plan runs.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--fresh` |  | start a new agent even when the task's could be resumed |
| `--plan <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--task <id>` |  | id of the task in the plan |

- `--plan` is required
- `--task` is required
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# A task of a plan of the project you are in
wdx plan task retry --plan sso --task schema

# With --fresh, as JSON
wdx plan task retry --plan sso --task schema --fresh --json
```

### Output

The task. With `--json`: {"result": "retried", "task": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `retried`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_not_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_not_running) | 1 | the plan is not running or paused |
| [`task_state`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#task_state) | 1 | the plan's task is not in a state the request needs |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx plan update

Write a plan's YAML as a new revision.

```sh
wdx plan update (--id <id> | --name <name>) [--project-id <id> | --project-name <name>] (--path <file> | --path -) --base <n> [flags]
```

`--base` is the revision the change was made on, as plan get printed it. If the plan has a newer revision, nothing is written: get it again, apply the change to it and update with the new base, so that no change is lost. The YAML is checked and reduced as in plan create; YAML that comes to the latest revision's makes none.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--base <revision>` | `0` | the revision the change was made on |
| `--id <id>` |  | id of the plan |
| `--name <name>` |  | name of the plan (case-insensitive) |
| `--path <file>` |  | file holding the new YAML, - for stdin |
| `--project-id <id>` |  | id of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |
| `--project-name <name>` |  | name of the project (default: the one the working directory is in) |

- `--base` is required
- `--path` is required
- exactly one of `--id` or `--name`
- at most one of `--project-id` or `--project-name`

### Examples

```sh
# Write back a changed copy
wdx plan update --name sso --path sso.yaml --base 2

# From stdin, as JSON
wdx plan update --id doc-1a2b3c4d --path - --base 2 --json
```

### Output

The plan's revision now, each after dropped, and the plans it lists moved to its folder. With `--json`: {"result": "updated", "plan": {...}, "dropped": [...], "moved": [...]}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `updated` or `unchanged`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`invalid_argument`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_argument) | 1 | an argument is empty or malformed |
| [`invalid_plan`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#invalid_plan) | 1 | the plan's YAML has problems: details.problems lists them |
| [`not_found`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#not_found) | 1 | nothing has this name or id |
| [`plan_changed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_changed) | 1 | the plan has a newer revision than the base given |
| [`plan_started`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#plan_started) | 1 | the plan has run: only a draft can be changed or run |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
